pages.text: $(l)2.5 million years ago.$() The marginal Homo beside habilis, with hands of its own: flakes and choppers, yes - but never the multi tool, and it never learned there was marrow in a bone. That goes for you too, as one.

$(l)Every kind$(): leafy twigs from a tree, one in each hand and $(k:hominin_evolution.item_interact) - a piece of $(l)nest$(). Two rocks in the crafting grid - a $(l)hammerstone$(). Hold $(k:hominin_evolution.item_interact) with a bare stick to gnaw a $(l)sharpened stick$(); fish a termite mound or dead wood with a plain stick for a $(l)termite stick$().

$(l)Stone$() - a rock in hand, a hammerstone in the other, $(k:hominin_evolution.item_interact): a $(l)flake$(), a $(l)chopper$(), a $(l)grinding stone$(), but not the multi tool: your kind's hands do not know it. Limestone will not take an edge: soft stone makes Lomekwian cores.

$(l)Two hands$() ($(k:hominin_evolution.item_interact)): a stick and a flake - a $(l)pointy stick$(). A long branch and a flake - a $(l)sharpened spear$(). A rock and a flake - a $(l)chopper$(). A long branch and a chopper - a $(l)digging stick$(). Two sticks - a $(l)fire drill$(). Each has to be worked out first.

Raw meat in hand, a flake in the other: $(l)four chunks$(). A worn stone tool in hand, a grinding stone in the other: an edge put back. A bone you can only gnaw the scraps off - your kind never breaks one open. An egg with a sharpened stick in the other hand: drink it, and keep the $(l)eggshell$() for water.
